_comment: Language registry. Breadth is configuration, not code: adding a language is a row here, never a code change. `validated` must be set from evidence — `npm run diag` proves the provider accepts the codes, field testing proves the model handles a real apprentice. The UI labels every unvalidated entry as a preview.

spitch.tts: POST /v1/speech — {text, voice, language, format, speed} -> audio
spitch.probed: 2026-10-08: ha, yo, ig and en round-trip (TTS -> ASR) cleanly. Nigerian Pidgin is asymmetric — translate takes `pcm`, speech takes `pi`; `pcm`, `npe`, `en-NG` and `pidgin` are all rejected by the speech endpoint. Both codes are recorded below. Re-run `npm run diag` after any provider change.

languages.name: Nigerian Pidgin
languages.notes: Widest reach among artisans and the natural register for trade talk, and the hardest ASR case: heavy accent plus trade jargon. The lexicon bias list matters most here.

languages.name: Hausa
languages.notes: Large, underserved northern artisan networks. Round-trips cleanly on the provider; still needs a trainer and three learners.

languages.name: Yoruba
languages.notes: Best-documented language on the provider, so the lowest-risk choice if Pidgin underperforms in field testing.

languages.name: Igbo
languages.notes: Maps directly onto the igba-boi apprenticeship structure the product is built around.

languages.name: English
languages.validatedBy: Source language — the authority all other locales are translated from
languages.notes: English wording is the reference. Every other locale is a translation of it and says so on screen.
